title: Ghost Hand
synopsis: This is Part 4 of our rendition of “Ghost Hand”.

fullText.simplified:
这个时候，朱龙开口道：“霍先生，你的面子真不小。据我所知，我们李时先生从来不让别人碰他的小宝物。你是第一人呢！”
    霍桑听后，半开玩笑地说道：“既然这样，我得先洗洗手才好。”他用两个指头从主人手里接过了金链，问：“洗手间在哪儿？”
    李时指了指洗手间的方向，霍桑转身去了洗手间。
    不一会儿，霍桑从洗手间出来，笑着说：“报告李先生。我不但洗手了，我还用了你们洗手间里的香皂，认认真真地洗了。”李时点点头，似乎很满意他的做法。
    霍桑坐回沙发上，打开小布袋，把那个宝物拿了出来。真的就是一条做工十分简单的小金龙，没有什么特别的地方。
    霍桑看着这条小金龙，心想：这么奇怪的东西，祖先那么认真地传到子孙手里。除了辟邪这个可笑的理由，应该还有别的理由吧？
    想到这，霍桑问：“能不能说说你曾祖父的事情？”
    李时不知道为什么这位大侦探要突然问起他曾祖父的事情，但还是把他以前听他父亲说的有关曾祖父的事情告诉了霍桑。

    李时的曾祖父名叫李单，曾在海军当官，做得很不错。他因为工作的关系，去过很多国家，在德国住的时间最长。因为他和晚清最有名的政治家李鸿章是好朋友，回国后，他曾向李鸿章提出过一个伟大的建议，但李鸿章当时没有听他的话。他很失望地回了老家，不再当官了。
    因为在李单之前，他们村里从来没有出过当大官的人，也从来没有人出过国，所以村里面的人对他有很多传说。
    其中一个传说是：李单从德国带回了很多颗钻石。钻石多得数不清，可以够他们李家人吃喝玩乐好几百年。全村人都相信李家藏有很多钻石，就连李家人也这么认为。这么多年来，李家的子孙们一直想找到钻石，但是直到现在，他们一颗都没有找到。
    李单死的时候，已经六十一岁了。那正是甲午战争战败的一年。当战败的消息传到李单那里时，他大叫了一声，倒在地上，当时就得了急病，快死了。家人们坐在他身边，问他还有没有什么话要说。他那时候已经说不了话了。他抬起他无力的手，指了指自己的耳朵，费尽全身力气，说出了一个“聋”字，这样一连说了好几次。最后，他又低低地叫着“大同”两个字。大同是他孙子的名字，也就是李时的父亲。
    当时，家人们认为他说的是他的耳朵聋了，听不见家人们的问话。但是看他紧张的样子，像是有什么重要的话还没说出来似的。于是，家人们跑去拿笔和纸，想让他写下来。老人用他那无力的手，很努力地拿起笔，在纸上写出了一个字。家人们费了好长时间，才看出老人写的那个字是“聋”字。
    最后，这位老人摇摇头，放下笔，死了。直到现在，家人们都不知道老人最后想要说的到底是什么。

    李时一口气把曾祖父的故事讲完了。霍桑看着他手里的那条小金龙，心想：这小金龙到底有什么秘密呢？如果它不重要，为什么老人要把这个东西传给自己的子孙呢？小金龙——“龙”，老人死前写的最后一个字——“聋”。“聋”可以分成两个字——“龙”和“耳”，那有没有可能老人本来想写的就是两个字——“龙”和“耳”呢？如果这个想法是对的，“龙”应该就是这条小金龙了，那么，“耳”又是什么意思呢？
fullText.traditional:
這個時候，朱龍開口道：“霍先生，你的面子真不小。據我所知，我們李時先生從來不讓別人碰他的小寶物。你是第一人呢！”
    霍桑聽後，半開玩笑地說道：“既然這樣，我得先洗洗手才好。”他用兩個指頭從主人手裡接過了金鏈，問：“洗手間在哪兒？”
    李時指了指洗手間的方向，霍桑轉身去了洗手間。
    不一會兒，霍桑從洗手間出來，笑著說：“報告李先生。我不但洗手了，我還用了你們洗手間裡的香皂，認認真真地洗了。”李時點點頭，似乎很滿意他的做法。
    霍桑坐回沙發上，打開小布袋，把那個寶物拿了出來。真的就是一條做工十分簡單的小金龍，沒有什麼特別的地方。
    霍桑看著這條小金龍，心想：這麼奇怪的東西，祖先那麼認真地傳到子孫手裡。除了辟邪這個可笑的理由，應該還有別的理由吧？
    想到這，霍桑問：“能不能說說你曾祖父的事情？”
    李時不知道為什麼這位大偵探要突然問起他曾祖父的事情，但還是把他以前聽他父親說的有關曾祖父的事情告訴了霍桑。

    李時的曾祖父名叫李單，曾在海軍當官，做得很不錯。他因為工作的關係，去過很多國家，在德國住的時間最長。因為他和晚清最有名的政治家李鴻章是好朋友，回國後，他曾向李鴻章提出過一個偉大的建議，但李鴻章當時沒有聽他的話。他很失望地回了老家，不再當官了。
    因為在李單之前，他們村裡從來沒有出過當大官的人，也從來沒有人出過國，所以村裡面的人對他有很多傳說。
    其中一個傳說是：李單從德國帶回了很多顆鑽石。鑽石多得數不清，可以夠他們李家人吃喝玩樂好幾百年。全村人都相信李家藏有很多鑽石，就連李家人也這麼認為。這麼多年來，李家的子孫們一直想找到鑽石，但是直到現在，他們一顆都沒有找到。
    李單死的時候，已經六十一歲了。那正是甲午戰爭戰敗的一年。當戰敗的消息傳到李單那裡時，他大叫了一聲，倒在地上，當時就得了急病，快死了。家人們坐在他身邊，問他還有沒有什麼話要說。他那時候已經說不了話了。他抬起他無力的手，指了指自己的耳朵，費盡全身力氣，說出了一個“聾”字，這樣一連說了好幾次。最後，他又低低地叫著“大同”兩個字。大同是他孫子的名字，也就是李時的父親。
    當時，家人們認為他說的是他的耳朵聾了，聽不見家人們的問話。但是看他緊張的樣子，像是有什麼重要的話還沒說出來似的。於是，家人們跑去拿筆和紙，想讓他寫下來。老人用他那無力的手，很努力地拿起筆，在紙上寫出了一個字。家人們費了好長時間，才看出老人寫的那個字是“聾”字。
    最後，這位老人搖搖頭，放下筆，死了。直到現在，家人們都不知道老人最後想要說的到底是什麼。

    李時一口氣把曾祖父的故事講完了。霍桑看著他手裡的那條小金龍，心想：這小金龍到底有什麼秘密呢？如果它不重要，為什麼老人要把這個東西傳給自己的子孫呢？小金龍——“龍”，老人死前寫的最後一個字——“聾”。“聾”可以分成兩個字——“龍”和“耳”，那有沒有可能老人本來想寫的就是兩個字——“龍”和“耳”呢？如果這個想法是對的，“龍”應該就是這條小金龍了，那麼，“耳”又是什麼意思呢？

sentences.pinyin: quán cūn rén dōu xiāng xìn lǐ jiā cáng yǒu hěn duō zuàn shí
sentences.english: Everyone in the entire village was convinced that the Li family was hiding a lot of diamonds.

sentences.simplified: 就连李家人也这么认为。
sentences.traditional: 就連李家人也這麼認為。
sentences.pinyin: jiù lián lǐ jiā rén yě zhè me rèn wéi
sentences.english: Even the Li family believed it was like this as well.

sentences.simplified: 这么多年来，李家的子孙们一直想找到钻石，
sentences.traditional: 這麼多年來，李家的子孫們一直想找到鑽石，
sentences.pinyin: zhè me duō nián lái lǐ jiā de zǐ sūn men yì zhí xiǎng zhǎo dào zuàn shí
sentences.english: So many years had gone by, and the descendants of the Li family always wanted to try to find the diamonds.

sentences.simplified: 但是直到现在，他们一颗都没有找到。
sentences.traditional: 但是直到現在，他們一顆都沒有找到。
sentences.pinyin: dàn shì zhí dào xiàn zài tā men yì kē dōu méi yǒu zhǎo dào
sentences.english: But to this day, they hadn’t found a single one.

sentences.simplified: 李单死的时候，已经六十一岁了。
sentences.traditional: 李單死的時候，已經六十一歲了。
sentences.pinyin: lǐ dān sǐ de shí hou yǐ jīng liù shí yī suì le
sentences.english: When Li Dan died, he was already 61 years old.

sentences.simplified: 那正是甲午战争战败的一年。
sentences.traditional: 那正是甲午戰爭戰敗的一年。
sentences.pinyin: nà zhèng shì jiǎ wǔ zhàn zhēng zhàn bài de yì nián
sentences.english: That was the exact year when the First Sino-Japanese War was lost.

sentences.simplified: 当战败的消息传到李单那里时，
sentences.traditional: 當戰敗的消息傳到李單那裡時，
sentences.pinyin: dāng zhàn bài de xiāo xi chuán dào lǐ dān nà lǐ shí
sentences.english: When news that the war was lost reached Li Dan's location, ..

sentences.simplified: 他大叫了一声，倒在地上，当时就得了急病，快死了。
sentences.traditional: 他大叫了一聲，倒在地上，當時就得了急病，快死了。
sentences.pinyin: tā dà jiào le yì shēng dǎo zài dì shang dàng shí jiù dé le jí bìng kuài sǐ le
sentences.english: .. he cried out loudly, fell to the ground, and at the same time he got acutely ill and was soon dying.

sentences.simplified: 家人们坐在他身边，问他还有没有什么话要说。
sentences.traditional: 家人們坐在他身邊，問他還有沒有什麼話要說。
sentences.pinyin: jiā rén men zuò zài tā shēn biān wèn tā hái yǒu méi yǒu shén me huà yào shuō
sentences.english: The family members sat by his side and asked him if there was anything he wanted to say.

sentences.simplified: 他那时候已经说不了话了。
sentences.traditional: 他那時候已經說不了話了。
sentences.pinyin: tā nà shí hou yǐ jīng shuō bù liǎo huà le
sentences.english: By then he was already unable to speak.

sentences.simplified: 他抬起他无力的手，指了指自己的耳朵，
sentences.traditional: 他抬起他無力的手，指了指自己的耳朵，
sentences.pinyin: tā tái qǐ tā wú lì de shǒu zhǐ le zhǐ zì jǐ de ěr duo
sentences.english: He lifted his powerless hand and pointed to his own ear.

sentences.simplified: 费尽全身力气，说出了一个“聋”字，
sentences.traditional: 費盡全身力氣，說出了一個“聾”字，
sentences.pinyin: fèi jìn quán shēn lì qi shuō chū le yí ge lóng zì
sentences.english: By exhausting all the strength in his body, he uttered the single word “deaf”.

sentences.simplified: 这样一连说了好几次。
sentences.traditional: 這樣一連說了好幾次。
sentences.pinyin: zhè yàng yì lián shuō le hǎo jǐ cì
sentences.english: He said it like this a good number of times in a row.

sentences.simplified: 最后，他又低低地叫着“大同”两个字。
sentences.traditional: 最後，他又低低地叫著“大同”兩個字。
sentences.pinyin: zuì hòu tā yòu dī dī de jiào zhe dà tóng liǎng ge zì
sentences.english: Finally, he also lowly cried out the two syllables in the word “Datong”.

sentences.simplified: 大同是他孙子的名字，也就是李时的父亲。
sentences.traditional: 大同是他孫子的名字，也就是李時的父親。
sentences.pinyin: dà tóng shì tā sūn zi de míng zi yě jiù shì lǐ shí de fù qīn
sentences.english: Datong was the name of his grandson, and also Li Shi’s father.

sentences.simplified: 当时，家人们认为他说的是他的耳朵聋了，
sentences.traditional: 當時，家人們認為他說的是他的耳朵聾了，
sentences.pinyin: dāng shí jiā rén men rèn wéi tā shuō de shì tā de ěr duo lóng le
sentences.english: Then, the family believed that what he said was that his ears had gone deaf, ..

sentences.simplified: 听不见家人们的问话。
sentences.traditional: 聽不見家人們的問話。
sentences.pinyin: tīng bu jiàn jiā rén men de wèn huà
sentences.english: .. and that he wasn’t able to hear the family’s question.

sentences.simplified: 但是看他紧张的样子，像是有什么重要的话还没说出来似的。
sentences.traditional: 但是看他緊張的樣子，像是有什麼重要的話還沒說出來似的。
sentences.pinyin: dàn shì kàn tā jǐn zhāng de yàng zi xiàng shì yǒu shén me zhòng yào de huà hái méi shuō chū lái shì de
sentences.english: But looking at his tense appearance, it seemed like there still was something important that he hadn’t said.

sentences.simplified: 于是，家人们跑去拿笔和纸，想让他写下来。
sentences.traditional: 於是，家人們跑去拿筆和紙，想讓他寫下來。
sentences.pinyin: yú shì jiā rén men pǎo qù ná bǐ hé zhǐ xiǎng ràng tā xiě xia lai
sentences.english: Consequently, the family ran to get hold of a pen and paper, and wanted to get him to write it down.

sentences.simplified: 老人用他那无力的手，很努力地拿起笔，在纸上写出了一个字。
sentences.traditional: 老人用他那無力的手，很努力地拿起筆，在紙上寫出了一個字。
sentences.pinyin: lǎo rén yòng tā nà wú lì de shǒu hěn nǔ lì de ná qǐ bǐ zài zhǐ shang xiě chū le yí ge zì
sentences.english: The old man used that powerless hand of his, picked up the pen with much effort, and wrote out a character on the paper.

sentences.simplified: 家人们费了好长时间，才看出老人写的那个字是“聋”字。
sentences.traditional: 家人們費了好長時間，才看出老人寫的那個字是“聾”字。
sentences.pinyin: jiā rén men fèi le hǎo cháng shí jiān cái kàn chū lǎo rén xiě de nà ge zì shì lóng zì
sentences.english: The family spent a good long while before they could see that the word that the old man had written was “deaf”.

sentences.simplified: 最后，这位老人摇摇头，放下笔，死了。
sentences.traditional: 最後，這位老人搖搖頭，放下筆，死了。
sentences.pinyin: zuì hòu zhè wèi lǎo rén yáo yáo tóu fàng xià bǐ sǐ le
sentences.english: Finally, this old man shook his head, put down the pen, and died.

sentences.simplified: 直到现在，家人们都不知道老人最后想要说的到底是什么。
sentences.traditional: 直到現在，家人們都不知道老人最後想要說的到底是什麼。
sentences.pinyin: zhí dào xiàn zài jiā rén men dōu bù zhī dào lǎo rén zuì hòu xiǎng yào shuō de dào dǐ shì shén me
sentences.english: To this day, no one in the family knows what last words the old man wanted to say in the end.

sentences.simplified: 李时一口气把曾祖父的故事讲完了。
sentences.traditional: 李時一口氣把曾祖父的故事講完了。
sentences.pinyin: lǐ shí yì kǒu qì bǎ zēng zǔ fù de gù shi jiǎng wán le
sentences.english: Li Shi told the story of his paternal great-grandfather to completion in one go.

sentences.simplified: 霍桑看着他手里的那条小金龙，心想：
sentences.traditional: 霍桑看著他手裡的那條小金龍，心想：
sentences.pinyin: huò sāng kàn zhe tā shǒu lǐ de nà tiáo xiǎo jīn lóng xīn xiǎng
sentences.english: Huo Sang looked at that small golden dragon in his hand, and thought to himself:

sentences.simplified: 这小金龙到底有什么秘密呢？
sentences.traditional: 這小金龍到底有什麼秘密呢？
sentences.pinyin: zhè xiǎo jīn lóng dào dǐ yǒu shén me mì mì ne
sentences.english: So when all is said and done, what is the secret of this small golden dragon?

sentences.simplified: 如果它不重要，为什么老人要把这个东西传给自己的子孙呢？
sentences.traditional: 如果它不重要，為什麼老人要把這個東西傳給自己的子孫呢？
sentences.pinyin: rú guǒ tā bú zhòng yào wèi shén me lǎo rén yào bǎ zhè ge dōng xi chuán gěi zì jǐ de zǐ sūn ne
sentences.english: If it’s not important, why did the old man want to pass on this thing as a gift to his descendants?

sentences.simplified: 小金龙——“龙”，老人死前写的最后一个字——“聋”。
sentences.traditional: 小金龍——“龍”，老人死前寫的最後一個字——“聾”。
sentences.pinyin: xiǎo jīn lóng lóng lǎo rén sǐ qián xiě de zuì hòu yí ge zì lóng
sentences.english: Small golden dragon – “dragon”. The last character that the old man wrote before he died – “deaf”.

sentences.simplified: “聋”可以分成两个字——“龙”和“耳”，
sentences.traditional: “聾”可以分成兩個字——“龍”和“耳”，
sentences.pinyin: lóng kě yǐ fēn chéng liǎng ge zì lóng hé ěr
sentences.english: The character “deaf” can be divided into two characters – “dragon” and “ear”.

sentences.simplified: 那有没有可能老人本来想写的就是两个字
sentences.traditional: 那有沒有可能老人本來想寫的就是兩個字
sentences.pinyin: nà yǒu méi yǒu kě néng lǎo rén běn lái xiǎng xiě de jiù shì liǎng ge zì
sentences.english: Is there a possibility then that it was just these two characters that the old man originally wanted to write ..

sentences.pinyin: lóng hé ěr ne
sentences.english: .. “dragon” and “ear”?

sentences.simplified: 如果这个想法是对的，“龙”应该就是这条小金龙了，那么，“耳”又是什么意思呢？
sentences.traditional: 如果這個想法是對的，“龍”應該就是這條小金龍了，那麼，“耳”又是什麼意思呢？
sentences.pinyin: rú guǒ zhè ge xiǎng fǎ shì duì de lóng yīng gāi jiù shì zhè tiáo xiǎo jīn lóng le nà me ěr yòu shì shén me yì si ne
sentences.english: If this train of thought is correct, “dragon” must be this small golden dragon. So, what did he then mean by “ear”?

sentence_translations: At this time, Zhu Long opened his mouth to say:
“Mr. Huo, you have a really big reputation.
To the best of my knowledge, our Mr. Li Shi never lets other people touch his little treasure. You’re the first one!”
When Huo Sang heard this, he half jokingly said: “Since it’s like that, I should wash my hands first.”
He took the offered gold chain from the owner’s hand with two fingers, and asked:
“Where is the washroom?”
Li Shi pointed in the direction of the washroom, and Huo Sang turned around and went to the washroom.
Not a moment later, Huo Sang came out from the washroom, and said with a smile:
“To inform Mr. Li.
Not only did I wash my hands, I also used the perfumed soap in your washroom, to wash them conscientiously.”
Li Shi nodded and seemed very pleased with his actions.
Huo Sang sat back on the sofa, opened the small pouch, and took out that treasure.
It really was a completely ordinary hand made small golden dragon, there was nothing special about it.
Huo Sang looked at this small dragon, and thought to himself:
Such a strange thing for the ancestors to pass down so earnestly to their descendants.
Apart from this ridiculous reason to ward off evil spirits, there must be some other reason?
Thinking about this, Huo Sang asked: “Can you tell me about your paternal great-grandfather’s circumstances?”
Li Shi didn’t know why this great detective suddenly started asking about his paternal great-grandfather’s circumstances.
But he still told Huo Sang what he’d heard his father say before concerning the paternal great-grandfather’s circumstances.
Li Shi’s paternal great-grandfather was called Li Dan, and was once a government official in the navy, doing really well.
He went to many different countries because of work, and lived the longest time in Germany.
Because he was a good friend of the most famous statesman in the late Qing dynasty Li Hongzhang, ..
.. after he returned to the home country, he once proposed a grand suggestion to Li Hongzhang.
But at that time Li Hongzhang didn’t listen to what he had to say.
He returned to his home region very disappointedly, and didn’t act as a government official anymore.
Because they in the village hadn’t ever produced someone that had been a big government official before Li Dan, ..
.. and never someone that had gone outside the country either, ..
.. the people in the village therefore had a lot of stories about him.
This was one of these stories: Li Dan brought back a lot of diamonds from Germany.
The diamonds were countlessly many, enough so they in Li family could eat, drink and be merry for hundreds of years.
Everyone in the entire village was convinced that the Li family was hiding a lot of diamonds.
Even the Li family believed it was like this as well.
So many years had gone by, and the descendants of the Li family always wanted to try to find the diamonds.
But to this day, they hadn’t found a single one.
When Li Dan died, he was already 61 years old.
That was the exact year when the First Sino-Japanese War was lost.
When news that the war was lost reached Li Dan's location, ..
.. he cried out loudly, fell to the ground, and at the same time he got acutely ill and was soon dying.
The family members sat by his side and asked him if there was anything he wanted to say.
By then he was already unable to speak.
He lifted his powerless hand and pointed to his own ear.
By exhausting all the strength in his body, he uttered the single word “deaf”.
He said it like this a good number of times in a row.
Finally, he also lowly cried out the two syllables in the word “Datong”.
Datong was the name of his grandson, and also Li Shi’s father.
Then, the family believed that what he said was that his ears had gone deaf, ..
.. and that he wasn’t able to hear the family’s question.
But looking at his tense appearance, it seemed like there still was something important that he hadn’t said.
Consequently, the family ran to get hold of a pen and paper, and wanted to get him to write it down.
The old man used that powerless hand of his, picked up the pen with much effort, and wrote out a character on the paper.
The family spent a good long while before they could see that the word that the old man had written was “deaf”.
Finally, this old man shook his head, put down the pen, and died.
To this day, no one in the family knows what last words the old man wanted to say in the end.
Li Shi told the story of his paternal great-grandfather to completion in one go.
Huo Sang looked at that small golden dragon in his hand, and thought to himself:
So when all is said and done, what is the secret of this small golden dragon?
If it’s not important, why did the old man want to pass on this thing as a gift to his descendants?
Small golden dragon – “dragon”. The last character that the old man wrote before he died – “deaf”.
The character “deaf” can be divided into two characters – “dragon” and “ear”.
Is there a possibility then that it was just these two characters that the old man originally wanted to write ..
.. “dragon” and “ear”?
If this train of thought is correct, “dragon” must be this small golden dragon. So, what did he then mean by “ear”?
